name: Task
first: A unit of work that runs an async closure, at the same time as the code that made it, which that code can wait for or cancel.

dependsOn.why: A task runs async code, which can suspend while it waits, from code that may not be able to wait.
dependsOn.whyInExample: The function `pack()` is async, as `makeTea(cups:)` is, and the task calls it with `await`.

sil.shows: The closure of the task on line 7 first moves to the executor of the main actor, which runs code on the main thread, as the top-level code does.
The executor that the closure moves to is the one of MainActor.shared, the main actor.

what.is: A task is a unit of work that runs an async closure, at the same time as other code. Writing `Task` before a closure makes one, as line 7 does, and the task starts by itself: no code calls it to start. The task's `value` is what its closure returns, which other code waits for with `await`.
what.afterExample: Line 7 makes a task that packs, and line 10 runs before the packing starts. Line 11 then waits for the task's result.
what.problem: Synchronous code, such as the action of a button, cannot call an async function, because it cannot wait. A task can: it is made from any code, runs the async work, and lets the code that made it go on without waiting.
what.how: Apple's documentation says that a task can start running right after it is made, and that it runs whether or not code keeps a reference to it. Keeping it, as `work`, lets code wait for its result, or cancel it. Here the top-level code and the task's closure both run on the main thread, so the closure starts when the top-level code waits.

when.text: Use a task to start async work from code that is not async, such as the action of a button.
Don't make a task inside an async function only to wait for it at once. Call the async function with `await` instead.

parts.name: The task, lines 7 to 9
parts.text: The closure after `Task` is the work that the task runs. It is async, so it can call `pack()` with `await`. What it returns, `"packed"`, becomes the task's result.

parts.name: The result, line 11
parts.text: The property `value` of `work` is the task's result. Reading it with `await` waits until the task has finished, then gives what the closure returned.

steps.text: Line 7 makes a task, which will run the closure on lines 7 to 9. The closure runs on the main thread, as the top-level code does, so it waits to start.
The top-level code goes on, and line 10 prints {{task started}}.
Line 11 waits for the task's result, so the top-level code suspends, and the task's closure starts. It calls `pack()`, and line 2 prints {{packing}}.
Line 3 suspends `pack()` for a tenth of a second, and line 4 returns `"packed"`, which is the task's result.
The task has finished, so line 11 goes on, and prints the result: {{packed}}.

end.text: The task ran its async work while the top-level code went on, and the top-level code got the result by waiting for `work.value`.
